channel.title: Federal News Network - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Federal News Network (federalnewsnetwork.com)

item.title: Federal employee retirement applications hit another record high
item.description: In February, another 31,000 retirement claims entered the Office of Personnel Management's systems.

item.title: CISA delays cyber incident reporting town halls due to shutdown
item.description: CISA had been planning to hold the town halls starting on Monday. The shutdown is "likely" to also delay issuance of the final cyber incident reporting rule.

item.title: DHS funding fight at home and conflicts abroad are pushing Congress into another week of high‑stakes maneuvering
item.description: "When you think about it, it's really one or two votes that make or break any legislation now in the House of Representatives," said Mitchell Miller.

item.title: Action needed to avoid memory loss
item.description: Industry and government are aware of the memory chip shortages and the resulting increase in prices. Doing nothing is not an option.

item.title: Woytek to leave NASA after 48 years
item.description: Joanne Woytek, the program director of the NASA SEWP program, which reached $12 billion in sales last year, has led the contracting effort since 1999.

item.title: U.S. organizations should prepare for cyber retaliation as conflict with Iran escalates
item.description: "[T]his is about making sure that you are ready for it because it's not a question of if, it's a question when," said James Turgal.

item.title: NIH sets up camp near one of the worst environmental disasters ever
item.description: "We'd like this to be a model moving forward for how community concerns can be integrated into research priorities," said Dr. Ashlinn K. Quinn.

item.title: AI company Anthropic sues Trump administration seeking to undo ‘supply chain risk’ designation
item.description: Anthropic is suing the Trump administration, asking federal courts to reverse the Pentagon’s decision designating the artificial intelligence company a “supply chain risk” over its refusal to allow unrestricted military use of its technology. Anthropic filed two separate lawsuits Monday, one in California federal court and another in the federal appeals court in Washington, D.C., each challenging different aspects of the Pentagon’s actions against the company. item.title: After deep staffing cuts, agencies seek mix of hiring and AI tools to rebuild capacity
item.description: The General Services Administration is looking at AI tools to help meet its mission, after losing nearly 40% of its workforce.

item.title: Lawmakers question DoD’s growing use of equity investments to strengthen DIB
item.description: Lawmakers want a detailed report on how DoD is monitoring those investments and what it plans to do with its ownership stakes.
